requirements.statement: `codex:tests.test_account_settlement_driver` and the two modules split out of it, `codex:tests.test_account_settlement_recovery` and `codex:tests.test_account_settlement_lifecycle`, each total at most 45 s, measured as the sum of the module's fragments' seconds (what the budget check counts), with full-run parallelism (`--jobs 16` beside `codex:tests.test_project_driver` and `root:test_install`).
no assertion is removed or weakened. Every changed assertion, renamed test, moved test or changed fixture behaviour is paired old -> new in [`testspeed3/assertions.md`](testspeed3/assertions.md).

the separate dispatch processes of one settlement test class share one bytecode cache outside the source tree (`dispatch_pycache`, opt-in), so only the first compiles the runtime; the dispatch arguments are unchanged.

the review-round class `ReviewRoundOneDriverTests` runs from `test_account_settlement_recovery`, and `ClosureAuthorityTests`, `StatusAgreementTests` and `LostLifecycleLimitTests` from `test_account_settlement_lifecycle`, on the same harness (imported, not copied); every test runs exactly once, in one module or another, and is registered in the layer, stage and requirement tables.

the settlement tests wait for a successor host's sweep in tenths of a second: their harness runs the project driver's sweep every 0.1 s instead of every second; no deadline, retry or fence rule of the product changes, and no test asserts the one-second cadence.
